NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers periodic manual inspection at depot intervals.
CALCULATED: Standard practice outcome class is MONITORING/INDICATION scheme.
USER CONSTRAINT: Proposed mechanism must be same class as standard practice.
ASSUMPTION: Standard practice mechanism is time-based interval inspection without continuous monitoring.
CALCULATED: Our mechanism departs by using acoustic signature analysis of early-stage crack propagation rather than visual inspection.
ASSUMPTION: Subsurface crack propagation generates detectable acoustic emissions before visible spall formation.
PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING PHYSICAL RELATION: Acoustic emission energy (AE) is proportional to crack surface area growth rate (dA/dt) and material fracture toughness (Kc). AE ∝ Kc² × E × dA/dt, where E is Young's modulus.
MAGNITUDE VERIFICATION: Bearing steel fracture toughness ≈ 50 MPa√m, Young's modulus ≈ 200 GPa. A 1 mm² crack growing at 0.1 mm²/day generates AE energy ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ J, detectable by sensitive microarrays at 1-10 kHz frequency range.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL
COMPONENTS (all off-the-shelf, same class as existing wayside station):
1. Wayside acoustic station microphone array (existing)
2. Wheel-impact-load-detector (existing)
3. Signal processing unit (same class as existing wayside data acquisition systems)
4. Crack-growth-rate analysis software (new algorithm, but standard signal processing class)
5. Temperature correlation module (existing data processing class)
PROCEDURE:
1. Acoustic data from microphone array is filtered to 1-10 kHz range (bearing-specific crack frequency range)
2. Wheel-impact-load-detector data identifies axles with abnormal impact signatures
3. Signal processing unit calculates crack growth rate from acoustic emission burst characteristics
4. Crack-growth-rate analysis software compares against material fatigue models
5. Temperature correlation module verifies if crack growth rate correlates with eventual temperature rise
BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
INSTALLABILITY: SAME - uses existing wayside infrastructure, no additional hardware required
OPERABILITY: SAME - integrates with existing wayside monitoring systems
MAINTENANCE: SAME - software updates only, same maintenance class as existing systems
COST CLASS: SAME - no additional hardware costs, only software development
EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL:
1. Install test system on 100 freight wagons with known bearing wear conditions
2. Monitor acoustic emissions continuously for 6 months
3. Record all acoustic events and correlate with wheel-impact data
4. Track actual bearing temperature measurements (when available)
5. Compare predicted failure dates with actual failures
INSTRUMENTS:
- Wayside acoustic station microphone array
- Wheel-impact-load-detector
- Portable temperature verification device (spot checks)
PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: Must predict bearing failure at least 60 days before critical temperature rise with >85% accuracy
DURATION: 6 months minimum monitoring period
KILL CRITERION: If fewer than 85% of bearing failures are predicted at least 60 days in advance, the mechanism is falsified
